(1) Gradient boosting machines (GBMs) and random forests are the most accurate classification methods for time series; (2) GBMs and random forests are also the most accurate outlier detectors for time series; and (3) there is no single best algorithm for outlier detection.

the problem of classifying time-series data.
how to use classification and outlier detection in real time systems.
the evaluation of classification and outlier detection algorithms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the choice of the best classification algorithm is data specific.
the choice of algorithms is task and data dependent, but we can derive some heuristics for the choice of algorithms.
Gradient Boosting Machines and Random Forest are the algorithms to try first for classification and outlier-detection, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can recommend Gradient Boosting Machines for classification, and Random Forest for outlier detection, when the time-series are short (less than 100 samples).
Gradient Boosting Machines and Random Forest are the best algorithms to use for both classification and outlier detection in time series data.
Gradient Boosting Machines, with the appropriate hyperparameters, are a good choice for both classification and outlier detection tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the accuracy of algorithms is highly dependent on the task and data.
there is no one algorithm that is best for all tasks and datasets.
we can use fast, scalable, and accurate algorithms to build systems that can learn from temporal data in a timely manner.
